title: Does APL Need a Type System? by Aaron W Hsu at #FnConf18
summary: Aaron Hsu's FnConf18 talk asks whether APL needs a static type system. He argues that APL's expressiveness and rapid iteration already deliver the benefits usually credited to types.
why: HN points to it as the main argument from the array-language camp that types are unnecessary there, and as a nuanced take on typed versus untyped programming.

quote.text: which argues that APL already provides the development ergonomics that are typically acribed to type systems.
